title: 2010 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: Equiangular hexagon \(ABCDEF\) has side lengths \[AB=CD=EF=1\] and \[BC=DE=FA=r.\] The area of \(\triangle ACE\) is \(70\%\) of the area of the hexagon. What is the sum of all possible values of \(r?\)

solutions.text:
Note that \(\triangle ACE\) is equilateral. Using the Law of Cosines in \(\triangle ABC,\) we get \(AC^2=r^2+1^2\) \(-2r\cos120^\circ\) \(=r^2+r+1.\)

The area of \(\triangle ACE\) is then \[ \dfrac{\sqrt3}{4} (r^2 + r + 1). \]

The three corner triangles \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\triangle CDE,\) and \(\triangle EFA\) each have area \(\frac12\cdot1\cdot r\cdot\sin120^\circ=\frac{r\sqrt3}{4}.\)

Thus the hexagon has area \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}(r^2+r+1)\) \(+3\cdot\dfrac{r\sqrt3}{4}\) \(=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}(r^2+4r+1).\)

The condition \([ACE]=70\%\cdot[ABCDEF]\) gives \[r^2+r+1=\dfrac{7}{10}(r^2+4r+1),\] so \(r^2-6r+1=0.\)

By Vieta’s formulas, the sum of the possible values of \(r\) is \(6.\)

Thus, E is the correct answer.
